notes.summary: PARTIAL: supplied actual-model energy–entropy recovery yields simultaneous interior P-level d_S and mixed-mass convergence in every dimension, discrepancy uniform integrability, and a joint large-time entropy limit from a fixed smooth Kähler start. The full residual P19.2 signature remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: On a fixed connected smooth compact Kähler manifold, use dd^c=i/(2pi), t=-log|tau|², full probability entropy and the actual usual NA datum. Starting from the supplied model recovery theorem, a common upper maximal ray gives d1(r_j(t),r(t))≤tB_j, B_j→0, and integrated Legendre top-mass error ≤B_j. Interior masses converge uniformly on compact level intervals. DDNL's ordered-envelope criterion then gives all-dimensional interior d_S and mixed-mass convergence. Recovered finite discrepancy moments imply discrepancy-tail uniform integrability. Actual model rays from a fixed smooth Kähler initial potential satisfy H(r_j(t))/t→H_NA(phi) along every joint limit j,t→∞. Singular initial points have only the stated A_j+tB_j d1 estimate. These are narrower simultaneous approximation results, not completion of unchanged P19.2.
notes.text:
The entire unchanged original P19.2 remains unresolved. The standalone partial paper is P19.2-paper.tex, with readable companion P19.2-argument.md and exact source applications in source-application-ledger.json.

Fix a connected smooth compact Kähler n-fold X, a Kähler form omega, alpha=[omega], V=∫omega^n and reference probability mu0=omega^n/V. Use dd^c=i/(2pi)∂∂bar, squared-log time t=-log|tau|², log-square divisor coefficients, normalized energy E(0)=0 and full probability entropy H=Ent(MA|mu0). The NA carrier is X^beth over C with trivial valuation; retain semivaluation supports. Discrepancy is over X: A_X(v_triv)=0 and its normalized Gauss component coefficient is (a+1-b)/b, where a is relative canonical order and b=ord(tau).

The supplied mathematical premise R is used exactly: for phi∈E1_NA(alpha) with H_alpha(phi)=∫A_X MA_alpha(phi)<∞, actual smooth equivariant relatively Kähler cohomological configurations eta_j exist with eta_j→phi strongly and H_alpha(eta_j)→H_alpha(phi). An actual model is a smooth dominating Y→X×P1 with real vertical divisor D, rho_X*alpha+D relatively Kähler, datum f_D(F)=ord_F(D)/b_F and compatibility U+log|s_D|²=O(1). R is the mathematical result in Section 5 of the supplied paper, not an inference from a historical PASS. Its construction uses effective vertical special-Fujita errors, Kähler classes beta_k, volume recovery, fixed positive-product recovery and the essential canonical-error limit beta_k^n K_Yk/Xcal→0. It supplies no extra prescribed P-envelope theorem. This submission does not independently reprove that entire construction.

Exact external foundations used below are stated and checked in the paper. MPWN, Lemma 5.0.5, Theorem 5.2.2 and Theorem B (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1), in the same smooth compact Kähler signature, give strong continuity of energy, suprema and probability MA, the supporting energy inequality, and ∫|eta_j-phi| MA(psi)→0 for fixed psi∈E1_NA. MP, Theorem 5.1.7 and Lemma 5.3.1 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2), give actual maximal rays r(w,phi), order in both arguments, affine energy E(w)+tE_alpha(phi), and sup r(0,phi)_t=t sup phi. Analytic supporting inequalities, ordered d1 and I1≤C d1 are Darvas's finite-energy foundations (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.2072v2, Theorem 5.5 and energy identities). Its printed i∂∂bar convention uses potential u/(2pi), with energy and metric restored by 2pi/V.

For any strong eta_j→phi, put lambda_j=max(eta_j,phi) and B_j=2E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(eta_j)-E_alpha(phi). The supporting inequality gives 0≤E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(phi)≤∫|eta_j-phi| MA_alpha(phi)→0. Consequently B_j≥0 and B_j→0. The genuine maximal ray s_j=r(0,lambda_j) dominates r_j=r(0,eta_j) and r=r(0,phi). Triangle inequality and ordered affine energy give d1(r_j(t),r(t))≤tB_j. No pointwise maximum of rays is declared geodesic. For genuine w_j→w in analytic d1, the same argument gives d1(r(w_j,eta_j)_t,r(w,phi)_t)≤A_j+tB_j, where A_j=2E(max(w_j,w))-E(w_j)-E(w)→0. Convergence follows from the analytic supporting inequality and I1≤C d1.

For initial zero define chi_r(lambda)=inf_{t≥0}(r_t-t lambda), and its raw normalized mass M_r(lambda)=V^-1∫<omega_chi^n>. Assign mass zero to levels identically -∞; never probability-normalize a zero-mass level. The precise analytic Legendre theorem is DXZ, Theorem 2.6 and published formula (51) (https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/50355), with the complete nonpolarized proof in Darvas–Zhang, Theorems 3.7, 3.9 and Propositions 3.8, 3.10 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.08324v4). The interior-mass continuity proof is Darvas–Xia, Lemma 3.9 (https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf). In a Kähler background with minimal initial zero, these give P-model levels, cutoff lambda^+=sup phi and energy slope c_r=lambda^++∫_{-∞}^{lambda^+}(M_r-1). Interior mass is positive, continuous and nonincreasing. No polarized algebraic closure theorem is imported into a transcendental class.

The Legendre level sigma_j of s_j dominates the other two levels, so mass monotonicity gives M_sj≥M_rj,M_r. Choose a finite L above all three cutoffs and extend profiles by zero above their cutoffs. Each energy formula becomes c=L+∫_{-∞}^L(M-1); finite energy makes every negative-tail integral finite. Subtraction gives ∫(M_sj-M_rj)=E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(eta_j) and ∫(M_sj-M_r)=E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(phi). Therefore ∫_R|M_rj-M_r|≤B_j. For nonincreasing functions, L1 convergence implies convergence at each continuity point: sandwich the value by averages immediately to its right and left, pass to the limit, then shrink the averaging intervals. A finite grid gives uniform convergence on every compact interior interval. The same argument applies to M_sj.

This also recovers finer singularity data in every dimension. Write M_k(u)=V^-1∫omega^(n-k)<omega_u^k>. DDNL, Lemma 4.3 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.00839), says exactly: if u≤v, M_n(u)>0 and b>1 satisfies b^n M_n(u)>(b^n-1)M_n(v), then h=P_omega(bu+(1-b)v) is omega-psh. Its complete contradiction proof and contact-set estimate in Lemmas 4.4–4.5 were checked. Put d=M_n(v)-M_n(u). When b^n d<M_n(v), h/b+(1-1/b)v≤u. Mixed-mass monotonicity, multilinearity and positivity imply M_k(v)≥M_k(u)≥(1-1/b)^kM_k(v), hence 0≤M_k(v)-M_k(u)≤k/b. For 0<d<M_n(v)/2 choose b=(M_n(v)/(2d))^(1/n). The ordered singularity metric formula, DDNL Lemma 3.4, is d_S([u],[v])=(n+1)^-1Σ_k(M_k(v)-M_k(u)), giving d_S≤(n/2)(2d/M_n(v))^(1/n). If d=0, let b→∞. Apply this estimate to both levels below sigma_j. On a compact interior interval the limiting top mass has a positive minimum, while both ordered top-mass defects tend uniformly to zero. All mixed masses and d_S therefore converge uniformly there. At positive mass, zero d_S means equal ceilings, which equal the P-envelopes, by the same source's Theorem 3.3 and Proposition 2.6. This is a topology detecting P-equivalence; it is not exact indexwise P-equivalence or pole preservation.

Entropy recovery gives discrepancy uniform integrability. For weak probability measures nu_j→nu and nonnegative lower-semicontinuous A with converging finite integrals, Portmanteau applied to A∧M yields limsup_j∫(A-M)_+dnu_j≤∫A dnu-∫(A∧M)dnu→0. On {A>2M}, A≤2(A-M)_+. Control late indices by this bound, then the finite early set by its finite individual moments. Thus lim_R sup_j∫_{A>R}A dnu_j=0. Apply this to MA_alpha(eta_j) and A_X. This concerns discrepancy against changing NA measures, not analytic density convergence or finite-time entropy-density uniform integrability.

A joint analytic entropy limit holds from a fixed smooth Kähler initial point. MP Lemma 5.3.2 and the proof of Theorem 5.3.4 give a mixed-pairing error C epsilon^q R^(1-q), q=2^-n, for mean-normalized finite-energy slots and fixed smooth cohomological inputs. Here the slot distance is ≤CtB_j and J=O(t), uniformly in j. Mean restoration gives, for t≥1, |G(r_j(t))-G(r(t))|/t≤C(B_j^q+|sup eta_j-sup phi|+|E_alpha(eta_j)-E_alpha(phi)|+1/t). M=H+G is the full probability Mabuchi functional, with G=T_-Ric+Sbar E and Ric=-dd^c log omega^n. For one fixed compatible divisor test Psi, the same slot replacement gives |∫Psi_t MA(r_j(t))-∫Psi_t MA(r(t))|/t≤C_Psi B_j^q. Ray-slot constant changes vanish because the test's smooth cohomological input is zero; test constants cancel between probability measures. Signed inputs are differences of positive inputs on one fixed common model, so constants do not depend on the changing configurations eta_j.

The calibrated test slope is ∫f_C MA_alpha(phi). Our base flux is -rF_r/2=F_t, with no extra factor two. MP's i/pi, unsquared-time mixed convention is transported using background 2omega, potential r_{2s}, datum 2phi in class 2alpha, then t=2s. For singular slots, decreasing model approximation gives an initial energy error plus t times an NA energy error. Divide the Hölder bound by t, take the time limit first, then decrease the approximation. This reconstructs the needed singular mixed slope.

For one fixed dominating SNC model, central B=Σb_iE_i and C_Y=K_Y/(X×P1)+B_red-B, a smooth metric on K_Y/P1+B_red-B defines positive fiber volume mu_Y,t with Psi_t=log(mu_Y,t/mu0) compatible with C_Y. Locally tau=product z_i^b_i. Its logarithmic relative frame is product dz_i/z_i wedged with free differentials. Independent y_i=-log|z_i|² occupy a weighted simplex Σb_i y_i≤t+O(1), giving ∫mu_Y,t=O((1+t)^n), retaining all multiplicities. Ambient positive fiber volumes are dominated by this logarithmic volume. The associated PL test is A_X composed with the model retraction. SD's exact bounded residual Hessian theorem, Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1601.07659v2), gives for each actual model ray MA(r_j(t))≤C_j mu_Yj,t. The bounded density decomposition and calibrated pairing prove H^∞(r_j)=H_alpha(eta_j); Gibbs' entropy inequality gives the matching lower bound. Finite-index constants may depend on j.

BDL's exact convex lower-semicontinuous Mabuchi theorem on E1, Theorem 4.7 with zero twist (https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf), implies M(r_j(t))≤M(0)+t(H_alpha(eta_j)+G_alpha(eta_j)). Its printed operator is transported with u/(2pi); Ricci and scalar-curvature factors cancel the energy scaling, leaving entropy coefficient one. Strong continuity of fixed mixed energies and the uniform G estimate give the joint limsup H(r_j(t))/t≤H_alpha(phi). For the lower bound first fix one SNC test model. Gibbs and its volume estimate give H/t≥∫Psi_t MA(r_j(t))/t-O(log(1+t)/t). Replace its pairing uniformly by the target ray's, take the joint liminf, and only then take the directed supremum of fixed discrepancy tests. This gives H_alpha(phi). Every joint limit with j,t→∞ therefore equals H_alpha(phi). At fixed time the convex M bound passes by d1 convergence and lower semicontinuity; subtracting the target contracted-energy slope gives the same entropy slope for the target ray. For fixed smooth w use background omega_w and potentials r_t-w. Models and datum are unchanged, all rays start at this exact w, and the two smooth reference entropies differ by a uniformly bounded term. Singular w is outside this joint entropy theorem.

The resulting simultaneous theorem retains actual models, the genuine fixed smooth initial point, energy and NA entropy, all interior P-level d_S and mixed masses, the L1 mass profile, discrepancy tails, and joint rescaled analytic entropy. General endpoints, zero-mass prescribed levels, exact poles/indexwise envelopes, singular initial-point level and entropy signatures, and the full residual hybrid approximation assertion remain unproved. No conclusion for P19.3 or P19.4 follows.

notes.summary: An explicit relatively ample positive-discrepancy P1 model has complete ray, entropy and P-envelope formulas. Central-fiber translation preserves energy–entropy recovery but destroys a fixed positive-mass endpoint. This is an implication failure, not nonexistence of a successful approximation.
notes.detailedSummary: For rational 0<c<1, the smooth blowup model D=-cF has central degrees c and 1-c. Its actual ray satisfies E=-c²t/2, NA measure (1-c)delta_triv+c delta_ord0 and H_NA=c. Its endpoint P-model level has logarithm-square pole c and raw mass 1-c. Actual configurations D_j=D-B/j converge strongly with identical measures and entropies, but their fixed lambda=0 level is -infinity of raw mass zero. The moving cutoff -1/j retains the endpoint exactly. A constant sequence succeeds, so this does not refute the original residual existence target.
notes.text:
Use X=P1, omega=dd^c log(1+|z|²) of mass one, dd^c=i/(2pi), t=-log|tau|² and full probability entropy. Fix rational c∈(0,1). Let F be the exceptional divisor of the smooth equivariant blowup Y of (z,tau)=(0,0) in P1×P1, and set D=-cF.

Define F0(x)=x log x+(1-x)log(1-x), 0log0=0, rho=log|z|², and q_t(rho)=sup_{0≤x≤1}{x rho-F0(x)-t(c-x)_+}. Put u_t=q_t(rho)-log(1+e^rho). With A=c/(1-c), y=|z|², differentiation F0'(x)=log(x/(1-x)) gives q_t(log y)=log(1+ye^t)-ct for y<Ae^-t; c log y-F0(c) for Ae^-t≤y≤A; and log(1+y) for y>A. The pieces match in first derivatives. Thus omega+dd^c u_t is positive, u0=0 and -ct≤u_t≤0. Every finite-time potential is bounded. Its radial probability measure is dx, x=∂_rho q_t, with mass c on the inner disk, zero on the middle annulus and 1-c outside, and no interface atoms. The total local weights are semipositive of complex-Hessian rank at most one and locally C1,1 on compact noncentral annuli; their Bedford–Taylor square is zero.

Actual-ray recognition can be checked directly through the P-model levels. Minimization in time gives chi(lambda)=0 for lambda≤-c, w_(c+lambda) for -c<lambda≤0, and -∞ for lambda>0, where w_b(z)=b log y-F0(b)-log(1+y) when y≤b/(1-b), and zero outside. For -c<lambda<0 the minimizing time is max(0,log((c+lambda)/(1-c-lambda))-log y). At lambda=0 the decreasing time limit is w_c. The curvature of w_b is b delta0 plus omega on y>b/(1-b), without circle mass. Its non-pluripolar raw mass is 1-b and its log-square pole coefficient is exactly b.

Here is a direct P-envelope proof. For B=b/(1-b), any omega-psh competitor h≤0, h≤w_b+C has subharmonic local weight Q=h+log(1+y) with an atom at zero of coefficient at least b. Therefore Q-b log y is subharmonic, bounded above near zero and extends across zero. On y=B its upper boundary value is log(1+B)-b log B=-F0(b). The maximum principle gives Q≤b log y-F0(b) inside, hence h≤w_b everywhere. Since w_b itself is a competitor, P_omega[w_b]=w_b. The calculated parameter curve is decreasing, concave and upper semicontinuous, is zero below -c, has endpoint w_c, and is -∞ above zero. It is a bounded P-maximal test curve. Convex duality gives inverse Legendre transform u_t. The analytic bounded-test-curve theorem applies in this Kähler signature: Darvas–Zhang, Theorem 3.7 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.08324v4), and Darvas–Xia, Theorem 3.7 (https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf). Hence u is the actual bounded weak ray from zero.

The configuration is admissible and positive. In the chart z=s tau, its total local weight minus c log|tau|² is log(1+|s|²) for |s|²<A and c log|s|²-F0(c) in the adjacent region, with bounded matching remainders. The other blowup chart gives bounded compatibility after subtraction of c log|z|². Thus its actual usual datum is f_-cF, with values -c at the exceptional Gauss valuation ord0 and zero at the strict central component. Clearing c's denominator gives the relative Q-line bundle p1*O(1)-cF. Its central component degrees are c and 1-c, and every other fiber has degree one. Positive degrees on two projective lines meeting at a node give fiber ampleness: high powers' sections vanishing at the node extend by zero and separate points and tangent directions, while sections with a shared nonzero node value generate there. Stacks Lemma 37.50.3 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D2S, complete primary proof checked) gives relative ampleness for this proper morphism. Adding a positive base class gives a compact Kähler model class. The boundary nef case c=1 is excluded.

Both central multiplicities are one, so the model probability measure is (1-c)delta_vtriv+c delta_ord0. Since A_X(ord0)=1 and A_X(vtriv)=0, H_alpha(f_D)=c. Model energy is D²/2=-c²/2 because F²=-1 and p1*alpha·F=0. Analytically, ∂_t u_t=-(c-x)_+ at the maximizing x, so E'(u_t)=-∫_0^c(c-x)dx=-c²/2 and E(u0)=0. This agrees with the Legendre mass-integral energy formula.

The density relative to omega is one outside y>A, zero on the middle annulus and e^t(1+y)²/(1+e^t y)² on the inner disk. Substitution k=e^t y gives the exact entropy H(u_t)=ct+2∫_0^A[log(1+e^-t k)-log(1+k)]/(1+k)² dk. The integral is uniformly bounded for t≥0 and finite at every finite t. Thus H(u_t)/t→c. This is an actual positive-discrepancy calibration in the declared operator, time and divisor normalization.

Let B=Y0 be the full central fiber and D_j=D-B/j. These actual rational configurations retain relative ampleness. Their data eta_j=eta-1/j converge uniformly and strongly; their actual initial-zero rays are u_j(t)=u_t-t/j. Energies satisfy E_alpha(eta_j)=E_alpha(eta)-1/j. Their NA and analytic measures and entropies are identical to those of eta and u. But chi_j(lambda)=chi(lambda+1/j), so chi_j(0)=-∞ with raw mass zero, whereas chi(0)=w_c has positive raw mass 1-c and pole coefficient c. At the moving cutoff lambda_j=-1/j the endpoint is exactly w_c, with exactly mass 1-c. Zero mass is never probability-normalized.

This proves that actual strong energy–entropy model recovery alone does not imply fixed endpoint P-envelope or mass recovery. It is not a nonexistence theorem: the constant sequence eta_j=eta succeeds. Therefore it does not close original P19.2.

The complete standalone proof is in P19.2-paper.tex and P19.2-argument.md. check_models.py checks c=.25,.5,.75 and t=0,.5,2,8,32,128 using Simpson quadrature with 2000 panels and critical-time Legendre substitution. All 18 finite rows passed; maximum absolute error was 6.742384428548576e-13. At c=.5, the endpoint diagnostic records target mass .5, shifted fixed-level mass zero and moving-endpoint mass .5. These are numerical observations, not exhaustive results or analytic proofs. Rerun python check_models.py > calculation-output.txt; outputs are calculation-output.json and calculation-output.txt.

notes.summary: A positive true-ray energy defect obstructs maximal model recovery of the ordinary datum and true energy slope simultaneously. The transported polar Cantor ray has defect a²/2, but its infinite entropy and nonmaximality do not refute unchanged P19.2.
notes.detailedSummary: For an actual finite-energy weak ray u from w with datum phi and maximalization uhat=r(w,phi), delta=E_NA(phi)-(E(u1)-E(u0))≥0. Model maximal rays with w_j→w and eta_j→phi strongly have asymptotic normalized distance to u tending to delta, and energy slopes tending to E_NA(phi). The supplied Cantor ray transports consistently by u_new(t)=2v_old(t/2), with backgrounds unchanged, retaining datum zero, energy slope -a²/2, P-levels and infinite entropy. This excludes only the explicitly stated maximal-model/usual-datum mechanism, not every admissible approximation signature in original P19.2.
notes.text:
Let u be an actual canonical finite-energy weak ray on a smooth compact Kähler manifold, from its genuine initial point w, with actual usual datum phi∈E1_NA(alpha). In the normalization of n1 let uhat=r(w,phi)≥u. Write c_u=E(u1)-E(u0) and delta=E_alpha(phi)-c_u≥0.

Ordered d1 and affine energy give d1(uhat_t,u_t)=t delta exactly. Suppose a proposed approximation uses actual maximal model rays r_j=r(w_j,eta_j), with w_j→w in d1 and eta_j→phi strongly. By n1's common-upper-ray estimate, d1(r_j(t),uhat_t)≤A_j+tB_j, with A_j,B_j→0. Direct and reverse triangle inequalities yield delta-B_j-A_j/t≤d1(r_j(t),u_t)/t≤delta+B_j+A_j/t. For each j, both time liminf and limsup lie within B_j of delta, and therefore tend to delta as j→∞. No exchange of limits is needed. Every maximal model ray also has energy slope E_alpha(eta_j), tending to E_alpha(phi). If delta>0, such a sequence cannot recover the true energy slope c_u or converge to u in chordal distance while recovering the same usual datum strongly. This is a nonexistence theorem only for the precisely specified mechanism.

The frozen input supplies a complete analytic polar Cantor ray on X=P1×Y, Y any compact Kähler manifold, from zero, with a∈(0,1). Its old operator is dd_L^c=i/pi and time s=-log|tau|. Keep its background forms Theta unchanged and define u_new(t)=2v_old(t/2), psi_new=2psi_old. Then Theta+dd^c u_new(t)=Theta+dd_L^c v_old(t/2); total homogeneous Monge–Ampère currents and probability measures agree. Normalized energy satisfies E_new(2v)=2E_old(v), so E_new(u_t)=2[-a²(t/2)/2]=-a²t/2. Bounds become -at≤u_t≤0. Entropy at t equals old entropy at t/2, retaining infinite entropy slope.

Generic coefficients of 2U_old measured against log|f|² equal those of U_old against log|f|. Thus the true ordinary datum remains zero on every total-space divisor and its usual psh extension is zero. This is not an assigned replacement datum. New Legendre levels satisfy chi_new(lambda)=2chi_old(lambda), since inf_t[2v(t/2)-t lambda]=2inf_s[v(s)-s lambda]. Their prescribed polar P-envelopes and raw masses are retained with the transported operator and backgrounds. The supplied construction proves vanishing of total-space divisorial coefficients using integrability of every exponential power of the actual total potential, rather than only slice Lelong numbers.

The maximalization from zero of ordinary datum zero is the zero ray, with NA energy and discrepancy entropy zero. Hence delta=a²/2. Maximal model rays strongly recovering that datum have asymptotic normalized distance tending to a²/2 from the genuine Cantor ray, and cannot simultaneously recover its true energy slope.

The Cantor construction is a supplied mathematical premise, not a historical review130 verdict. It is P-maximal in test-curve terminology but nonmaximal for its ordinary datum and has infinite true entropy slope. Original P19.2 does not state that every such ray must be approximated by maximal models retaining only its ordinary datum. Thus this does not refute the full residual finite-entropy/log-discrepancy-model and prescribed-singularity existence regime. Retaining additional P-data may require a different mechanism; assigning a different datum to erase the defect would change the requested signature. No conclusion follows for P19.3 or P19.4.

The full proof and scope analysis are in P19.2-paper.tex and P19.2-argument.md; source-application-ledger.json distinguishes supplied data from fresh primary inputs. The extracted Cantor construction is cantor130-data.md. Rerun python build_paper.py > build-command-output.txt and python validate_deliverables.py > validation-output.txt. No finite computation is used as proof of this obstruction.
